answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks collateral that is slashed if it misbehaves, so a gale of cheap clones still costs real money per identity. Reputation then accrues slowly, like violet dye deepening over time, and cannot be bought instantly. An attacker facing umber-dark audit trails and a per-identity bond finds spawning thousands of Sybils unprofitable, since each one must pay up front and earn trust from zero.
